comments.author: @tommytuna1419
comments.text:
I’ve have a product I sell.  I was selling it for 2 years.  I made changes and now I have a full year from my first sale of the new design, or my first date of public knowledge(my YouTube video) to apply for a provisional patent.  After I file a provisional patent I then have another year to either get a full patent or just try to work with a bigger company to get this rolling.   
Remember to always have a paper trail with companies you are talking to, no one wants to have a bad reputation in the business world.  So if you have a long trail of paper work/ photos you should be fine-ish. I got stuck in the mind set of wanting all the profit for myself.  Get in the mind set of having your product first to market, the best way to do that is to work with a company that can make it happen.  It’s a lot of work, but I think it’s the way to go.  If you do get involved with a company, look for royalties and make sure those royalties are passed on in case the company sells to another company.  

If I am wrong, Stephen, please correct me.
